newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aborigine sues Australian state over bashing.
newsitem.headline: Aborigine sues Australian state over bashing.

text.p: An Aborigine is suing the Queensland state government claiming police assisted by a member of the U.S. marines used excessive force in arresting him, the man's solicitor said on Tuesday.
Sascha Blake, 19, is suing the Queensland government for A$50,000 (US$39,250) over his arrest in March outside a nightclub in Ipswich, 30 km (18 miles) east of Brisbane.
Blake was charged with using obscene language.
Blake claims he was bashed during the arrest, in which a visiting United States marine taking part in a joint Australia-U.S. military exercise helped police.

Blake's arrest was one of a number made by police which were captured by a video surveillance camera. The video footage broadcast on Australian television showed a man in the uniform of a U.S. marine using force to subdue Blake.
Local media have reported the man was a U.S. marine.
Blake's solicitor, Paul Richards, told Reuters his client did not intend to include the United States in the claim for compensatory, aggravated and punitive damages.
"The delay and additional expense likely to be incurred in pursuing a foreign country mean that it would not be worth it," Richards said.
A United States official said the U.S. defence force was helping local authorities with their inquiries into the incident.
